q: What is demurrage in railway terminology?

options.B: A discount on freight for bulk loading of wagons
options.C: A tax imposed on all goods carried by rail
options.D: A penalty for late running of goods trains

options.A: Increase the freight revenue of the railways
options.B: Ensure quick release and faster turnover of wagons
options.C: Penalise consignors for late freight payment
options.D: Recover the cost of goods shed maintenance

options.B: The date of manufacture of goods

q: What is the basic purpose of free time in demurrage rules?

options.B: A reasonable loading or unloading period before detention charges.
options.D: Time allowed to dispute freight bills.

q: When does demurrage normally begin to accrue on a wagon?

options.A: When the wagon enters railway premises.
options.C: When the consignee applies for delivery.
options.D: After wagons are placed and permitted free time ends.

q: How is demurrage best distinguished from wharfage?

options.A: Demurrage is wagon detention; wharfage is occupation of railway wharf space.

q: What event normally starts free time for unloading at a goods shed?

options.C: Placement of wagons and availability for unloading.

q: Why are holidays and Sundays important in demurrage calculation?

options.B: They may be included in free time unless rules provide otherwise.
options.D: They are ignored in every detention case.

q: If a wagon is detained continuously across a Sunday, what should the station do?

options.A: Stop the clock automatically on Sunday.
options.B: Treat Sunday as extra free time.
options.C: Waive charges because offices are closed.
options.D: Count time under applicable free-time rules, not assumptions.

q: What does congestion detention require before demurrage is enforced?

options.A: Examination of who caused and controlled the detention.

q: How should railway-caused placement delays be handled in demurrage claims?

options.A: Ignore them and bill full detention.
options.C: Verify records and allow appropriate relief if detention was not the party's fault.

q: What is wharfage primarily charged for?

options.B: Use of railway wharf or land for keeping goods beyond free time.

q: When does wharfage normally begin on goods in a shed?

options.D: After free time for removal expires.

q: How does demurrage end when goods are unloaded but remain in the shed?

options.A: It stops when the wagon is released, while wharfage or storage may begin.

q: What is the key conceptual difference between stacking charges and demurrage?

options.A: Stacking is freight; demurrage is wharfage.
options.C: Stacking concerns goods occupying space; demurrage concerns wagon detention.

q: Why may parcels and goods have different wharfage treatment?

options.D: Because traffic class can determine separate free-time and charge frameworks.

q: What should a station verify before raising a demurrage bill?

options.B: Placement time, free time, removal or release time, and detention records.

q: Which record is most important for defending a demurrage charge in a dispute?

options.A: A complete wagon detention register with timings.

q: What makes a demurrage waiver accountable?

options.C: Written approval by the competent authority with reasons recorded.

q: What should happen to waivers that exceed a station's powers?

options.B: Send them upward with facts and recommendations.

q: How should frequent routine waivers be viewed in audit?

options.D: As a warning sign of weak control or misuse.

q: What is the correct treatment of unpaid demurrage at a station?

options.A: Pursue recovery and report outstanding amounts through proper channels.

q: When can excess demurrage be refunded?

options.C: When records show overcomputation or wrong application, with approval.

q: What should a consignee's demurrage dispute include?

options.D: A written claim supported by timings and documents.

q: Why should oral assurances not settle demurrage disputes?

options.B: They lack verifiable evidence and accountability.

q: How do crane charges interact with demurrage?

options.A: They are separate charges; crane use does not itself stop detention time.

q: If crane breakdown delays unloading, what should the station establish?

options.A: That demurrage must always be charged.
options.C: Whether delay was beyond the party's control and supported by records.

q: What is shed detention in the demurrage context?

options.B: Detention of wagons at a goods shed beyond free time.

q: What happens if unloading finishes but the empty wagon is not released?

options.D: Detention may continue until the wagon is released.

q: Why is transit delay different from demurrage?

options.A: Demurrage concerns terminal or siding detention beyond free time, not running time.

q: What should be done if loading continues after free time expires?

options.C: Charge demurrage for detention beyond free time.

q: How should partial unloading affect demurrage?

options.B: Detention continues until wagons are actually released.

q: What if a consignee refuses delivery of goods?

options.C: The station must absorb the loss.
options.D: Detention liability continues until lawful disposal or release.

q: Which audit check best tests completeness of demurrage revenue?

options.A: Comparing detention registers with bills raised and amounts collected.

q: What audit evidence supports a demurrage waiver?

options.C: Competent approval, recorded reasons, and supporting timings.

q: Why should demurrage bills be raised promptly?

options.D: To prevent disputes, accumulation, and revenue leakage.

q: What is a common audit finding in wharfage control?

options.B: Goods occupying railway land without timely billing.

q: How should disputes over free-time commencement be resolved?

options.A: By checking placement and availability records against rules.

q: What should a station do when detention was caused by siding congestion?

options.C: Record causes, verify responsibility, and process relief under competent authority.

q: Why must waiver decisions avoid favoritism?

options.D: Because selective relief undermines revenue control and fairness.

q: What is the station's accountability for demurrage refunds?

options.B: Verify error, obtain approval, and preserve audit trail.

q: How should repeated detention by the same party be handled?

options.A: Enforce charges consistently and escalate persistent problems.

q: What is the best summary of demurrage and wharfage control?

options.C: Accurate time records, prompt billing, competent waivers, and audit review.
